title: Seaborn: statistical graphics

spans.text: WHY USE THIS?

Seaborn was created under Michael Waskom's leadership to make statistical graphics easier to explore. It works naturally with pandas tables and builds on Matplotlib, which handles rendering and file output. Its dataset-oriented API maps columns to color, groups, and statistical summaries.
PURPOSE AND SETUP

A plot helps compare numbers quickly and spot trends or unusual measurements. Matplotlib and Seaborn create plots that can be shown on screen or saved to a file. Install the examples with `python -m pip install matplotlib seaborn pandas`.
RUNNABLE EXAMPLES
Example 1: compare average scores across classes with a bar chart.
QUESTION: What plot will this code create? Predict first, then run it.

spans.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns

scores = pd.DataFrame({
    'class': ['A', 'A', 'B', 'B', 'C', 'C'],
    'score': [70, 80, 75, 85, 82, 88],
})
sns.set_theme(style='whitegrid')
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
sns.barplot(data=scores, x='class', y='score', errorbar=None, ax=ax)
ax.set(title='Average score by class', xlabel='Class', ylabel='Score')
plt.show()
A bar chart titled "Average score by class" opens.

WHICH CHART SHOULD I CHOOSE?

• Relationships: `scatterplot` shows two numeric measures; `lineplot` shows ordered/time measures; `relplot` can split results into facets.
• Distributions: `histplot` bins values, `kdeplot` smooths density, and `ecdfplot` shows cumulative proportions; `displot` creates figure-level distribution charts.
• Categories: `barplot` estimates a summary (mean and uncertainty by default); `countplot` counts observations.
• Spread: `boxplot` shows quartiles and possible outliers, `violinplot` shows distribution shape, and `stripplot` / `swarmplot` show individual observations.
• Multiple variables: `heatmap` color-codes a table or correlation matrix; `pairplot` / `jointplot` explore pairs of variables.
Seaborn has no pie-chart function; use Matplotlib `ax.pie` for a few part-to-whole categories.

The charts use the axes returned by `fig, ax = plt.subplots()`. `plt.show()` opens a plot in an interactive environment; servers and automated tests should use `fig.savefig('chart.png', dpi=150)` and call `plt.close(fig)` when finished. `ax.set()` adds clear titles and axis labels.

spans.title: Watch out
spans.text: A name is not a copy of its value; mutations to a shared list or dictionary are visible through every alias.
COMMON MISTAKES
Distinguish a variable name, indentation, and comment: whitespace affects syntax, while comments explain intent.
